figures.caption: Fig. 1. The overview of the system. The system consists of three components, i.e., the data processing component, the model component, and the visualization component.
figures.rationale: This figure is a high-level architectural concept overview of the system's three core components, not an actual full system user interface, a single view panel, a user analysis workflow, concrete case study, or experimental evaluation result.

figures.caption: Fig. 2. The example of the structure of a match. M refers to ”Match”, Gi refers to ”Game”, Ri j refers to ”Rally”, and Si, j k refers to ”Stroke”. The red parts are newly added compared with the old model. (A) illustrates the division of the four phases.
figures.rationale: This figure illustrates the hierarchical structural concept of a match, explaining its phase division as a background data structure concept, which does not fit any of the other defined roles.

figures.caption: Fig. 3. The original model and the new model. Blue encodes the original model, red encodes the new model. (A) and (B) present the state vectors. Specifically, in (A), Sk represents the stroke, Vk represents the state vector of each stroke Sk, vi,p1 and vi,p2 represents the state value of stroke attributes and wp1 and wp2 represents the state value of winning of the two players. (C) presents the simulation process.
figures.rationale: This figure illustrates the conceptual structure of the original and new models, including their state vectors and simulation process, which is an algorithm/concept illustration that does not fit any of the other defined roles.

figures.caption: Fig. 4. The evaluation between the two models. The red lines represent the new model and the blue ones represent the old model.
figures.rationale: This figure is a precision-recall curve comparing performance between two models, which is an experimental evaluation result matching the description in the caption.

figures.caption: Fig. 5. The system interface. The donut charts and the pie charts encode the scoring rates and utilization rates, respectively. (A) is the player view which displays all matches of Ito Mima and her opponents. It provides navigation of matches. (B) is the tactic view which displays the tactics specified by stroke placement at the serve phase. It provides navigation of tactics. (C) is the simulation view which is under the exploration mode. It contains (D), the exploration component for implementation of adjustments and (E), the evaluation component for evaluation of adjustments. (D) displays all of the adjustment options specified by stroke placement and stroke technique. (E) displays the three optimum strategies generated by the system.
figures.rationale: This figure displays the complete full system interface of the Tac-Simur system, showing all coordinated main panels/views including player view, tactic view, and simulation view with its sub-components, matching the definition of an interface figure.

figures.caption: Fig. 6. The explanation mode of simulation view. (B) presents the correlation among strokes. (C) and (H) present the former and latter two strokes of the adjustment (E).
figures.rationale: This figure displays the explanation mode of a simulation view, which is a single local interface panel/component, not the full complete system interface, so it is classified as view.

figures.caption: Fig. 7. The figure of Section 6.2. (A) presents the tactics used by Ito Mima in the serve phase. (B) presents the adjustment strategies in the evaluation component. (C) presents explanation of the adjustments.
figures.rationale: This figure shows a concrete analysis walkthrough of a specific player's serve phase tactics, adjustment strategies, and related explanations, which is a concrete use example/analysis walkthrough matching the case_study role. It is not the complete full system interface.

figures.caption: Fig. 8. The figure of Section 6.3. (A) presents the tactics used by Ding Ning in the serve phase and (B) presents those in the receive phase. (C), (D), and (E) present adjustment strategies in evaluation component. (F) and (G) present the explanation of the adjustments.
figures.rationale: This figure shows Ding Ning's serve- and receive-phase tactic comparisons, simulated adjustment strategies, and explanations in the documented case study.
